root_cause.text: The use of `BUG_ON()` assertions in `sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence()` to validate dword-alignment of fence writeback addresses allows unprivileged userspace to trigger a kernel panic via crafted `DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS` submissions.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence() contains two BUG_ON(addr & 0x3) assertions... [which] can be reached from unprivileged userspace via crafted DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS submissions, causing a fatal kernel panic", which is supported by the patch diff replacing `BUG_ON(addr & 0x3)` with `WARN_ON(addr & 0x3)`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `sdma_v4_0_ring_emit_fence` contains `BUG_ON(addr & 0x3);` assertions on lines 442 and 452 to validate the dword-alignment of the fence writeback address. Since this address can be influenced by userspace via the `DRM_IOCTL_AMDGPU_CS` ioctl, an unprivileged user can trigger a kernel panic (denial of service) by submitting an unaligned address.
